content: Verified against docs.github.com 'Removing sensitive data from a repository': revoke/rotate the secret FIRST (rotation alone may make history rewrite unnecessary); removing from HEAD is insufficient since commits remain in history, clones, forks, and cached GitHub views reachable via SHA; GitHub officially recommends git-filter-repo (2.47+ has --sensitive-data-removal flag) and deprecated filter-branch; contact GitHub Support to remove cached views and run server-side GC; collaborators must re-clone or rebase (one merge commit can reintroduce tainted history); you cannot clean other users' clones or forks. Force-push rewrite changes commit hashes, breaks signatures and PR diffs.
